newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwandan Hutu refugee group denounces repatriation.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan Hutu refugee group denounces repatriation.

text.p: A Rwandan Hutu refugee lobby group said on Thursday repatriation of Rwandan refugees from Zaire was the last stage in a "Final Solution" to remove any Hutu threat to Rwanda's government.
The Rally for the Return of Refugees and Democracy in Rwanda (RDR) called for an international inquiry into genocide and crimes against humanity against Rwandan Hutu refugees in Zaire.
The Hutu refugees fled Rwanda in 1994 and are collectively accused by minority Tutsis of genocide in Rwanda the same year.

"The last broken pieces of the last episode in the implementation of the plan to break any political, economic, intellectual or military threat to the RPF (Rwanda Patriotic Front) regime in Kigali are being swept, picked and dumped in Rwanda under the U.N. repatriation exercise," the RDR said.

"The Rwandan people may not have the resources or the might to fight injustice meted out on it but sooner or later history will judge those who were behind or condoned the horrendous crimes committed against the Hutu population," the RDR added.
It said the final episode for the refugees began last week when refugee camps south of Kisangani city were attacked.

It said the plan for the attack, which was originally supposed to be carried out by Ugandan, Burundian and Rwandan forces but was later switched to Zairean forces, was approved by the Pentagon in the United States and British intelligence.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan last week called the dispersal of refugees a policy of "slow extermination", and a U.N. food agency spokeswoman, making a comparison with Hitler's Germany, said: "The expression 'Final Solution' is not exaggerated."
The RDR said the "Final Solution" for the refugees led to the repatriation of "ghosts" by U.N. agencies in an airlift.
"The world is now busy looking for funds to deliver them to the RPF. It is highly probable that many will die in Rwandan jails while others will be left to die licking their wounds," it said.

The U.N. refugee agency started an airlift in earnest back to Rwanda on Wednesday of some of the estimated 100,000 Rwandan refugees south of the northeastern Zairean capital of Kisangani. It says another 250,000 Rwandans are unaccounted for in Zaire.
The Rwandan government accused the United Nations on Thursday of delaying the repatriation of refugees and said it was ready to work directly with rebel forces in Zaire to bring them back.

Rwanda's jails and lockups are overcrowded with some 100,000 Hutus accused of killing in the genocide of 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates in 1994. Many of suspects returned from Tanzania and Zaire last year.
